newsitem.title: UK: UK jazz musician-club owner Ronnie Scott dies.
newsitem.headline: UK jazz musician-club owner Ronnie Scott dies.

text.p: Ronnie Scott, jazz musician and owner of London's best known jazz club, has died at the age of 69, friends said on Tuesday.

Scott died at his London home on Monday night -- but the show went on as usual at the Ronnie Scott's club in Soho which he launched in 1959. Staff at the club said Scott would have wanted performances to continue.
Ronnie Scott's grew from a basement with a second-hand piano to one of the most famous jazz clubs in the world hosting performers ranging from Count Basie to Coleman Hawkins.

Until last week Scott was still hosting acts at the club although he had recently stopped performing himself. He often introduced perfomers with the catchphrase "Quiet please, you're not here to enjoy yourselves."
"His death is a great loss to the jazz world," said James Parsons, a manager at the club.
"He was a very funny man as well as a fabulous musician. he was also very sincere, that is why people took to him so readily."
